item.title: What’s So New About the New Museum Building?
item.description: The Lower East Side institution's OMA-designed, $82 million expansion debuted this week to mixed reviews.

item.title: Hyperallergic’s Art Tarotscope for the Spring Equinox
item.description: The earth’s orbit around the sun continues unabated, reminding us that nothing is permanent, neither darkness nor light.

item.title: Israel Reportedly Considers Banning Artist and NYC First Lady Rama Duwaji
item.description: A state agency took issue with pro-Palestine art and “likes” on social media posts made by Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s wife, according to reports.

item.title: Artists Grapple With Cesar Chávez’s Legacy After Abuse Allegations
item.description: The farmworker movement led by Chávez and Dolores Huerta, one of his accusers, has been a central influence for generations of Latine and Chicano artists.

item.title: New Ways of Seeing at the Outsider Art Fair
item.description: This year’s edition proves that the key to viewing work by so-called “autodidact” artists is recognizing its capacity and merit as equal to all other art forms.

item.title: The Whitney Biennial Is for the Faint-Hearted
item.description: I got the sense that this biennial is hiding from the world today instead of reflecting on it.

item.title: Iranian Artist Speaks Her Heart
item.description: Plus: Impressions from the reopened New Museum, impending strike at NYU, Islamic futurism, the price of Egyptian blue, and much more.

item.title: Whitney Biennial Shies From the Moment
item.description: Our editor-in-chief's thoughts about the Whitney Biennial, John Yau remembers Thaddeus Mosley, the fallout from the allegations against Cesar Chávez, and more.

item.title: Before the “Global South,” Indian Modernists Dreamed of Solidarity
item.description: Historian Atreyee Gupta unravels the threads of catchall terms like “Global South” to trace the connections between Indian painters and anticolonial figures like Frantz Fanon.

item.title: Joel Meyerowitz on Photographing Giorgio Morandi’s Studio
item.description: “He was assembling a force field of geometric objects,” said Meyerowitz, whose book of images exploring the painter's famous still lifes is being rereleased this spring.

item.title: Trump Erects Contentious Columbus Statue Outside White House
item.description: The original was among dozens of Columbus monuments toppled in 2020 during nationwide protests against racial violence.

item.title: The Angel of History Is Stuck in Jerusalem
item.description: The iconic Paul Klee work is missing from an exhibition about fascism at the Jewish Museum in New York due to "current conditions" in Israel.

item.title: Is There an Ethical Path for AI Art?
item.description: There is a destabilizing, dreamlike sense of awe in encountering something without knowing the answer to sanity’s most fundamental question: “Is this real?”

item.title: White Girls and the Global South
item.description: Happy spring! If you've been stuck in a reading slump like me, look no further.

item.title: Columbus Statue at the White House
item.description: Trump installs a toppled Columbus statue outside the White House, a Paul Klee exhibition in New York opens without its centerpiece, and photos from Morandi’s studio in Bologna.
